reviewer: Codex (editorial primary-source review; not independent expert approval)

discovery.mechanism: AI can find a useful research lead; development accelerates only if that contribution relieves a bottleneck without losing time to validation or other stages.
discovery.conditions: Retain R1–R2 quality and bottleneck conditions and the separate successor-improves-development requirement for RSI.
discovery.counterexample: A promising computational lead can fail to reappear on reruns and still require extensive human analysis and laboratory work.
discovery.evidence: Read the technical report’s methods and limitations with its announcement and visually inspected Figure 1. The new record separates search, follow-up and unresolved function.
discovery.limits: No controlled whole-project speedup, biological function, independent replication or fully autonomous research claim is established.
discovery.mitigation: Preserve independent result checking, reproducibility tests and records of human work, costs and elapsed time at each stage.
discovery.readerContext: Both languages explain a research lead before its limits and distinguish finding, reproducing and experimentally validating it.
discovery.whyHere: The example informs R1 research assistance; its limitations explain why R2 and RSI do not follow automatically.

primary.support: A computational research lead, unsuccessful reruns and human-directed follow-up; not established biological function or whole-project acceleration.
Developer announcement distinguishes the agent campaign from subsequent human laboratory work.

oversight.mechanism: Access during development may reveal failures that finished-model testing misses; prevention also requires findings to lead to timely corrective action.
oversight.conditions: Actual access, adequate independence, reporting rights and a route to correction must accompany the announced partnership.
oversight.counterexample: An evaluator can be contracted without receiving sufficient access or causing a dangerous deployment to be stopped.
oversight.evidence: Compared Anthropic’s partnership announcement with the counterparty statement and retained bounded control-experiment evidence.
oversight.limits: An announcement is neither a completed audit nor measured reduction in incidents. Direct developer funding and unsettled standards are explicit.
oversight.mitigation: Verify practical access, publishable findings, corrections and outcome measures; continue permission limits and pre-execution checks.
oversight.readerContext: C3 introduces prevention; C3a1 explains the gap between tests and actual work before describing the proposed additional scrutiny.
oversight.whyHere: These additions update the external-evaluation proposal without changing the evidence level for control failure.

primary.locator: Access, funding, standards and intended evaluation work
primary.support: Announced developer-funded evaluation program; actual access, publication and effectiveness remain to be established.
Trusted monitoring/editing improves limited programming experiments under specified assumptions.

execution.mechanism: An unwanted choice can become an action when execution capability and access coincide with failed prevention; lasting loss of control requires additional persistence and spread.
execution.conditions: Preserve C1/C2/C3 for local failure and L/C4a/C4b for unrecovered control. Access, authorization, evaluation awareness and concealment remain distinct.
execution.counterexample: Human intervention can contain an unauthorized action. Awareness of a test can coexist with inability to circumvent restrictions.
execution.evidence: Revisited incident settings and investigation limits, bounded scheming results, a negative control result and the dated frontier assessment.
execution.limits: Incomplete logs and selected scenarios do not estimate representative incidence. Separate observations cannot establish all AND conditions in one event.
execution.mitigation: Keep independent action records, least privilege, monitor stress tests, human escalation and recoverable operations.
execution.readerContext: The explanatory order distinguishes selecting an action, being able to execute it, missed prevention and failure to regain control.
execution.whyHere: These boundaries prevent local incidents from being presented as demonstrated organization-wide or global loss of control.

primary.support: Permissive internet access and retrospective monitoring in a real evaluation; human intervention limits consequences.
Observed local coordination and attempts to obscure conduct, with incomplete records and a bounded investigation.

primary.locator: Assessment window, Key facts and risk-assessment scope
primary.support: February–March assessment separates local harmful opportunities from persistence under human intervention; not a September ceiling.
Evaluation awareness without the claimed ability to bypass testing restrictions; limited to the evaluated model and setup.
Elicited behavior under supplied goals and context does not measure ordinary deployment prevalence.
An available external transfer method was used without the required authorization.

capability.mechanism: Research can improve capabilities, but improvements must transfer to the required workflow before supporting reliable task completion or automation.
capability.conditions: Preserve transfer, exception handling, cost and intervention conditions. ASI requires broad substantial superiority, not success on one task family.
capability.counterexample: A model can solve a long software benchmark yet fail at unfamiliar work or interpersonal and physical requirements.
capability.evidence: Re-read METR’s measurement definition and extrapolation limits alongside ordinary training improvements in Chinchilla.
capability.limits: Human task duration is not autonomous runtime. Older measurements are not current capability ceilings or proof of RSI.
capability.mitigation: Test unfamiliar workflows, record assistance and interventions, and bound permissions separately from measured capability.
capability.readerContext: Explain whose task duration is measured and what work remains outside the test; avoid assuming readers know the benchmark.
capability.whyHere: Capability progress branches toward execution, work and safety research without requiring ASI or harmful intent.

primary.support: Measured human task duration for bounded tasks is distinct from agent runtime, complete occupations or broad superiority.
Finite-compute training improvements provide a path to capability gains without requiring a self-improvement loop.

work.mechanism: Task capability can support adoption; household outcomes then depend on actual production, labor demand, distribution and transition opportunities.
work.conditions: W1/W2 remain separate for all-labor replacement. W3/W6 govern access without labor income; complete labor replacement is not required.
work.counterexample: AI can augment employed workers or increase production while households that lose wages receive no compensating income.
work.evidence: Read exposure methods, robot-demonstration limits, adoption denominators, and economic-model caveats rather than converting them to a replacement probability.
work.limits: Selected physical demonstrations are not economy-wide reliability; older surveys and conditional scenarios are not forecasts of current universal adoption.
work.mitigation: Track actual income, essential consumption, adoption costs, job transitions and who receives productivity gains.
work.readerContext: Separate technical possibility, practical use, job loss and being able to live without wages in both route and detail text.
work.whyHere: The alternative economic branches explain why the same capability gains can have different effects across people and sectors.

primary.support: Measured human task duration for bounded tasks is distinct from agent runtime, complete occupations or broad superiority.
Task-based occupational exposure does not establish replacement or unemployment.

primary.locator: Demonstrations, human intervention and remaining challenges
primary.support: Physical-task demonstrations have unresolved reliability and practical deployment boundaries.
Firm and employment weighting differ; observed use includes augmentation and is not a causal estimate of job losses.
Conditional US scenarios distinguish adoption, displacement, augmentation and adjustment frictions; they are not probability-weighted predictions.
Adoption and ownership mediate wage and wealth outcomes in a calibrated model.

income.mechanism: Useful goods and authorized transactions can produce revenue; full costs and ownership determine profit and its recipients. Lower prices also depend on pass-through and supply constraints.
income.conditions: I1a/I1b stay joint conditions, while P1/P2 distinguish cheap production from access and allocation. Neither payment volume nor low cost alone determines outcomes.
income.counterexample: A store can record sales while depending on human approvals and labor, or cheaper production can leave scarcity and unequal purchasing power intact.
income.evidence: Re-read the store’s operating arrangements, payment-data scope, distribution-model summary and distinct functions of money.
income.limits: Developer demonstrations and funded payment analysis do not establish independent autonomous profitability or universal income gains.
income.mitigation: Record total costs, ownership, authorizations, liability, access to essentials and distribution rather than infer them from transaction volume.
income.readerContext: Define sales, profit, income and payment functions through the concrete questions each branch addresses.
income.whyHere: Income, cheaper goods and diminished reliance on monetary allocation are separate possibilities, not a single automatic chain.

primary.support: Human approvals and physical work remain; sales and operating results are not an autonomous full-cost business.

primary.locator: Method, data attribution and payment authorization discussion
primary.support: Observed payment activity is distinct from profit, demand and unrestricted authorization.
Ownership and adoption assumptions shape distributional outcomes; not an observed universal benefit.
Medium of exchange, accounting and saving are different functions, not an AI-driven disappearance forecast.

finance.mechanism: Important financial operations may transmit malicious behavior or correlated errors; system-wide disruption also requires defenses and buffers to fail.
finance.conditions: Keep F2a/F2b as overlapping alternatives and F1/F2/F4 as joint conditions. Persistent payment distrust needs additional failure of recovery.
finance.counterexample: Broad AI use may be supervised and improve compliance, while independent buffers and settlement systems prevent an operational failure from spreading.
finance.evidence: Revisited the financial-use survey and FSB vulnerability and monitoring analyses, with cyber-test settings kept separate from financial deployment.
finance.limits: Provider concentration is not trading correlation. Capability tests and potential vulnerabilities are not an observed AI-caused financial crisis.
finance.mitigation: Retain authority limits, stress tests, independent settlement and recovery, and measurement of dependencies and correlated decisions.
finance.readerContext: Use concrete lending, payment and household-access outcomes while distinguishing an institution’s AI use from autonomous critical operations.
finance.whyHere: The financial branch addresses a distinct route to disruption and does not imply that money disappears after a market shock.

primary.support: Respondent adoption and fully autonomous use cases have different denominators; concentration does not measure synchronized trading.
Potential correlated behavior, cyber risk and dependency can matter while efficiency and supervision may improve.
Indicators help examine concentration and vulnerabilities without establishing that an AI-caused systemic crisis occurred.

primary.locator: Cyber evaluation methods and dated results
primary.support: Known-vulnerability attempts and special evaluation settings do not measure successful attacks against finance in deployment.

context.mechanism: Research, execution and economic outcomes remain connected by conditional pathways rather than a single inevitable sequence.
context.conditions: Preserve AND/OR structure, research-cycle feedback, safety-research alternatives, distribution requirements and the additional transition from control loss to global harm.
context.counterexample: Useful research and improved oversight can coexist; task automation may augment work; local loss can be contained before it becomes systemic.
context.evidence: Read the dependent graphs, route summaries, story chapters and affected news/evidence context alongside the changed bilingual explanations.
context.limits: The new sources support individual claims and do not validate complete causal paths, estimate extinction risk or refresh every older source.
context.mitigation: Keep independently testable conditions, counterexamples and safeguards visible in the tours and standalone details.
context.readerContext: The tour first introduces the question that each branch answers; later exceptions do not assume knowledge of ASI, benchmarks or economic models.
context.whyHere: Dependent summaries must not turn narrowly scoped additions into stronger claims elsewhere in the service.

scope.mechanism: The update records new evidence and substantive scheduled reassessment, not new probabilities or whole-map certification.
scope.conditions: Advance only the 24 due nodes, five due edges, two additional edited nodes and reassessed C3 evidence date; preserve other dates and classifications.
scope.counterexample: An index visit or unrelated updated model card does not cause existing source metadata or every node to receive today’s date.
scope.evidence: The accompanying record lists accepted sources, actual primary-source passages, retained conclusions, counterevidence and excluded candidates.
scope.limits: This is a scoped daily review, not the Monday sweep or independent scientific replication. The JSON review is editorial, not human PR approval.
scope.mitigation: Validate content, translation and graph invariants; compare history translations by stable ID; keep the new daily proposal as a draft.
scope.readerContext: History explains the additions and their limits in both languages, separately from the previously authorized production release.
scope.whyHere: The date and history disclose what was assessed and why colors and causal conditions remain unchanged.
